sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: The post Gupta period is known for the progress in ______ architecture and sculpture.
At ______ we see the Pancharathas and Mandapa structures.
The Pallavas and Western Chalukyans are remembered for their ______ activities.
Chola artists excelled in ______ casting.
The Cholas and Hoysalas are always remembered for their ______ projects.

sections.passage: The Post Gupta period in India is known for the progress in temple architecture and sculpture. Major dynasties like Pallavas, Cholas, Hoysalas in the south and Palas, Senas and Gangas in the east patronized this progress. In the south, at Mahabalipuram or Mamallapuram, we see the Pancharathas and the Mandapa structures. While Pallavas and their rivals, Western Chalukyans are remembered for their sculptural activities, Cholas and Hoysalas would be always remembered for their temple projects. Chola artists excelled in the techniques of bronze casting. The Chola period has also given us temples like the Gangaikondacholapuram temple and the Brihadeswara temple. (October 2025)

sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: The Sun Temple at Konarka was built by King ______ of the Ganga dynasty.
It is situated near ______ in Orissa.
The larger images are usually of ______ stone.
The female musician figures are found on the ______ of the temple.
The Surasundari is shown playing a ______.

sections.passage: The Sun Temple at Konarka was built by King Narasimhadeva I of the Ganga dynasty on the eastern coast of India near Puri in Orissa. The temple is famous for its gigantic structure and larger than life size sculptures. The larger images, usually of black stone, have affinity with the later Bengal style of the Pala period. The female musician figures are found on the terraces. The Surasundari is shown with a drum. The slight tilt of the head and rhythmic actions of the limbs present the graceful beauty of this drummer.

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: The Hoysala dynasty emerged in the middle of the eleventh century.
The capital of the Hoysalas was Belur.
Hoysala sculptures show deep carving and undercutting.
Hard granite made deep carving possible in Hoysala sculpture.
questions.answer: False – the soft stone made it possible.

sections.passage: The Hoysala style is named after one of the famous dynasties of the Deccan, which emerged around the middle of the eleventh century and came to an end in the mid fourteenth century. The capital of the Hoysala kings was Dvarasamudra, the modern Halebid. The earliest major Hoysala temples are at Belur. Hoysala sculptures show deep carving and undercutting, soft rhythms of the body contours, delicate and intricate designs. Deep carving is made possible by the soft stone. (April 2025)

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: Arjuna's Penance is a relief on two huge boulders.
It belongs to the Chola period.
questions.answer: False – it belongs to the Pallava period.

questions.q: Another name of the relief is Gangavatarana.
The figures are shown facing away from the cleft.
questions.answer: False – all figures face the cleft.

sections.passage: Arjuna's Penance is a relief on two huge boulders at Mamallapuram, made in the Pallava period in the 7th century AD. There is a cleft between the two boulders and all figures face it. According to some scholars the relief is Gangavatarana, where Shiva receives the flow of the Ganges in his hair. Others think it should be known as Arjuna's Penance because a male figure is shown in meditation at one end. The animal figures, like the sleeping baby elephant and the deer scratching its nose, show the close observation of the artists.

questions.q: Hoysala period is remembered for the stone sculptures. Why?
questions.answer: Hoysala sculptures show deep carving and undercutting made possible by the soft stone, which gives a rich surface texture and intricate details. They have soft rhythms of the body contours and delicate designs, and the sculptures form an intrinsic part of the temple architecture.

or.q: Give a general introduction to Hoysala art.
or.answer: The Hoysala style is named after the Hoysala dynasty of the Deccan (mid 11th to mid 14th century); the capital was Dvarasamudra (Halebid) and the earliest major temples are at Belur. Temples were decorated with sculptures forming part of the architecture, with deep carving, undercutting, soft body rhythms and intricate designs.

questions.q: Name the capital of the Pallava dynasty rulers. Mention two main features of the statues made during this dynasty.
questions.answer: The capital was Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram). Pallava sculptures are gentle, soft and rounded, with enormous speed and monumentality; the animal figures show close observation of nature.

questions.q: Write a very short note on 'Krishna Supporting Mount Govardhana'.
questions.answer: It is a stone sculpture (about 3 ft) of the Hoysala period from Belur. Krishna stands as the central heroic figure with human beings and cattle shown in layers; the animals are lively and the figures have elaborate jewellery; deep carving shows the mastery of the artist.

questions.q: Describe the Surasundari from Konarka.
questions.answer: It is a little more than life-size stone figure of a female musician from the 12th-century Sun temple in Orissa, shown with a drum. The big smiling face, slight tilt of the head, rhythmic limbs, soft carving of ornaments and folds of drapery give graceful beauty and rhythm.

questions.q: Describe Arjuna's Penance in a few lines.
questions.answer: A Pallava relief (7th century AD) at Mamallapuram, about 91 ft x 152 ft, on two huge boulders with a cleft in between. Life-size gods, demigods, sages and animals face the cleft; some think it shows the descent of Ganga received by Shiva and others Arjuna's penance.

questions.q: Name two famous Chola temples and the metal in which Chola artists were expert.
questions.answer: Chola artists were expert in bronze casting; famous Chola temples are the Gangaikondacholapuram temple and the Brihadeswara temple, noted for simplicity, monumentality and majestic quality.

questions.q: Which temples were built by the Ganga rulers in Orissa?
questions.answer: The Mukteswar temple, the Lingaraja temple, the Rajarani temple and the Sun temple at Konarka.

sections.title: Short answer question. Answer in 50–60 words.

questions.q: What are the characteristics of the 'Krishna Supporting Mount Govardhana' sculpture? Where is it located?
questions.answer: It is located at Belur and belongs to the Hoysala period (stone, about 3 ft). Krishna is the central heroic figure with human beings and cattle in different layers, a stance with rhythmic limbs that brings softness; the animals are lively; there are heavy breasts and buttocks, elaborate jewellery and typical Indian hairstyle; deep carving and undercutting in soft stone show the mastery of the artist.

questions.q: What are the characteristics of the Konarka 'Surasundari' sculpture?
questions.answer: It is a little more than life size, in stone of the Ganga dynasty (12th century). The modelling is tight, the face broad with a smile, the work robust with loose plasticity. Female musicians on the terraces are boldly carved, full of movement and volume; the Surasundari is shown with a drum, with a slight tilt of the head, rhythmic limbs, soft ornament carving and rhythmic folds of drapery.

or.q: Where is the Sun Temple of Konark? What are the characteristics of the Konark sculptures?
or.answer: The Sun Temple stands at Konarka near Puri in Orissa; it was built by Narasimhadeva I in the form of a chariot. The sculptures are gigantic, larger than life size and usually of black stone, with tight modelling, broad smiling faces and robust bodies.

questions.q: Describe Arjuna's Penance or Gangavatarana.
questions.answer: It is a Pallava relief (7th century AD) on two huge boulders at Mamallapuram, about 91 ft x 152 ft, with a cleft between them. Life-size gods, demigods, sages and animals face the cleft; the upper part is full of movement and the lower part calm with meditating ascetics. It may show Shiva receiving the Ganga or Arjuna's penance. It has speed, monumentality and soft, round figures; animals like the sleeping baby elephant show close observation.

questions.q: Write the main characteristics of Hoysala sculptures.
questions.answer: They show deep carving and undercutting made possible by the soft schist stone, rich surface texture, soft rhythms of body contours and delicate intricate designs; sculptures are part of the temple architecture; examples are at Belur, Halebid and Somnathpur.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 70–80 words.

questions.q: Explain Arjuna's Penance (Gangavatarana): its medium, period, place, size and artistic features.
questions.answer: Arjuna's Penance is a stone relief of the Pallava period (7th century AD) at Mamallapuram near Chennai, about 91 ft x 152 ft, by an unknown artist. It is carved on two huge boulders with a cleft between them; life-size gods, demigods, sages and animals face the cleft. The upper part has movement and energy; the lower part is calm with meditating ascetics. Some scholars read it as Gangavatarana (Shiva receiving the Ganga in his hair) and others as Arjuna's penance. The figures are soft and round, the animals (baby elephant, monkeys, deer scratching its nose) show close observation, and it is a masterpiece of southern Indian sculpture.

questions.q: Write a note on Hoysala art with reference to the Krishna Govardhana sculpture.
questions.answer: The Hoysala style (mid 11th–mid 14th century) developed in the Deccan with capital Dvarasamudra (Halebid); major temples are at Belur, Halebid and Somnathpur. Temples were decorated with sculptures that form part of the architecture. The soft stone allowed deep carving and undercutting, soft rhythms and intricate details. The Krishna Supporting Mount Govardhana from Belur (about 3 ft) shows Krishna as the central heroic figure with humans and cattle in layers, lively animals, heavy breasts and buttocks, rich jewellery and typical hairstyle, showing the artist's mastery.
